column7: 2026-11-05: Decision (user's): when a Range header has more ranges than the new `limit` option on rangeParser, return a single range from the lowest start to the highest end (collapse/coalesce), NOT -2/-1/truncate/throw. Reason: their CDN can cache single-range responses but not multipart, and video players tolerate a few extra bytes. Context: download managers send hundreds of tiny ranges, which produce giant multipart responses. I had recommended returning -2 instead; the user chose collapse. Not yet implemented; next session writes it. Still open (not decided by user): whether limit counts raw comma-separated pieces or only valid ranges; whether combine runs before the limit check; the result must keep .type; limit unset = no limit (my suggestion, for backward compat). Update README Options and add tests.

2026-11-05: Implemented limit (collapse to one range, lowest start..highest end, type kept; unset = no limit). My choices, not the user's: limit counts only valid ranges (after parsing, not raw pieces), and runs after combine. README + tests done.
